correctness.rationale: Exact Z[phi] standard 600-cell coordinates establish 600 exposed tetrahedra; each yields three distinct opposite-edge pairings, giving 720 double vertices and 1800 distinct edges. The embedded 720-entry parent certificate has 719 verified parent edges, every chain terminating at the single root, proving connectivity. Finite-graph collapse proves the complete wedge of 1081 circles. Girth six is separately checked by exhaustive BFS. The exact standalone checker and finite parent certificate were replayed locally.

originality.rationale: The 2025 motivating primary full text establishes the double definition and a general connectivity bound but no 600-cell computation. Standard 600-cell graph sources refer to its 120-vertex skeleton, not to the 720-vertex edge-opposition graph. Public summaries of closest indexed double computations are limited to stacked 3-spheres, cyclic 4-polytope boundaries, multipartite complexes and polygon joins; none structurally includes this cell decomposition. Alias, parameter, equality and stronger-coverage queries revealed no directly covering result. Some primary texts remain inaccessible, and priority is best-knowledge only.
residual_risks: Full text of the closest publicly indexed stacked-sphere and cyclic-polytope notes was unavailable; comparisons are limited to stated hypotheses and published summaries.
An equivalent edge-opposition graph computation may be indexed under a different name or appear in an unindexed graph table; absence from searched records does not prove priority.

value.rationale: The regular 600-cell is a canonical exceptional triangulated 3-sphere; its doubling is a natural construction and is not known to be connected from the general theorem. Contrast with disconnected doubles of other polytopal 3-spheres motivates the exact connectivity question. Proving it determines an entirely new integral homotopy and free fundamental group with 1081 loops; a fully explicit spanning tree and girth-six graph description support reuse, rather than an arbitrary low-motivation numerical slice.
